final_sql:
SELECT s.street AS "Street", s.city AS "City", s.zip AS "Zip", s.state AS "State"
FROM satscores sa
JOIN schools s ON sa.cds = s.cdscode
WHERE sa.numtsttakr > 0
ORDER BY CAST(sa.numge1500 AS REAL) / sa.numtsttakr ASC, sa.cds ASC
LIMIT 1
answer: The school with the lowest excellence rate (NumGE1500 / NumTstTakr = 0) is located at 2607 Myrtle Street, Oakland, CA 94607-3415. Note that 18 schools tie for the lowest excellence rate of 0% (no test takers scored 1500 or above); this one is returned first when ties are broken by the school's CDS code.
clarifying_question: There are 18 schools tied with an excellence rate of exactly 0%. Which one should be reported, or is a full list of the tied schools preferred?
assumptions: Excludes schools with NumTstTakr = 0 or null to avoid division by zero.
When multiple schools tie at the minimum excellence rate (0%), the school with the smallest CDS code is chosen as a deterministic tiebreaker.
Uses the unabbreviated Street field (not StreetAbr) for the address.

final_sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT s.school, s.county, sc.avgscrread,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY s.county ORDER BY sc.avgscrread DESC) AS rnk
  FROM schools s
  JOIN satscores sc ON s.cdscode = sc.cds
  WHERE s.virtual = 'F' AND sc.avgscrread IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT school FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 5 ORDER BY county, rnk
answer: Among schools that are exclusively virtual (Virtual = 'F') and have SAT reading scores recorded, only four exist in the dataset, and each one ranks in the top 5 for average reading score within its own county: California Virtual Academy @ Los Angeles and Insight @ Los Angeles (Los Angeles County), Capistrano Connections Academy (Orange County), and California Connections Academy @ Ripon (San Joaquin County).
assumptions: Virtual schools are those coded 'F' (Exclusively Virtual) per the hint.
Only schools with a recorded SAT average reading score (join to satscores) are considered; schools with no SAT data are excluded from ranking.
Ties in average reading score are handled with RANK() so equal scores can share a rank within top 5.

final_sql:
SELECT atom_id, element
FROM atom
WHERE atom_id IN ('TR144_8', 'TR144_19')
ORDER BY atom_id;
answer: The bond TR144_8_19 connects atom TR144_8, which is carbon (c), and atom TR144_19, which is hydrogen (h).

final_sql:
SELECT m.molecule_id, COUNT(a.atom_id) AS atom_count
FROM molecule m
JOIN atom a ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id
WHERE m.label = '-'
GROUP BY m.molecule_id
HAVING COUNT(a.atom_id) > 5
ORDER BY m.molecule_id
answer: There are 186 non-carcinogenic molecules (label = '-') that have more than 5 atoms. Examples include TR060 (103 atoms), TR059 (102 atoms), TR131 (82 atoms), TR438 (73 atoms), TR305 (71 atoms), and many others — the full list of 186 molecule IDs with their atom counts is returned by the query.
assumptions: Interpreted 'consisted more than 5 atoms' as COUNT of atoms (rows in atom table) per molecule_id being greater than 5, as stated in the hint.
Only molecules with label exactly '-' are considered non-carcinogenic; molecules with null label are excluded.

final_sql:

Percentage is computed as (count of foreign_data rows with language='Chinese Simplified') / (total count of foreign_data rows) * 100, per the hint's formula applied to the table containing the language column.

final_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT l.format, l.status
FROM cards c
JOIN legalities l ON c.uuid = l.uuid
WHERE c.name = 'Benalish Knight'
ORDER BY l.format
answer: The card "Benalish Knight" is Legal in 8 formats: Commander, Duel, Legacy, Modern, Pauper, Penny, Premodern, and Vintage. It has no banned or restricted status in any format listed.

Since multiple printings (uuids) of the same card name exist, duplicate rows are removed via DISTINCT since all printings share the same legality status per format.

final_sql:
SELECT p.publisher_name
FROM hero_attribute ha
JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
JOIN superhero s ON ha.hero_id = s.id
JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Speed'
ORDER BY ha.attribute_value ASC
LIMIT 1
answer: The slowest superhero (lowest Speed attribute value, 5) is Franklin Storm, who was published by Marvel Comics.
assumptions: Interprets 'slowest superhero' as the single hero with the minimum Speed attribute value (a unique minimum of 5 was found).

final_sql:
SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL)*100/COUNT(*) AS pct_female_marvel
FROM superhero s
JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id=g.id
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id=p.id
WHERE g.gender='Female'
answer: About 54.68% of female heroes were published by Marvel Comics.
assumptions: Female heroes are those joined to gender.gender = 'Female' via gender_id.
Percentage is computed as (count of female heroes published by Marvel Comics) / (total count of female heroes) * 100.

JOIN races ra ON r.raceid = ra.raceid

answer: The fastest lap speed recorded among all drivers in the 2009 Spanish Grand Prix was approximately 202.484 km/h.

final_sql:
WITH champion AS (
  SELECT ds.driverid
  FROM driverstandings ds
  JOIN races r ON ds.raceid = r.raceid
  WHERE r.year = 2009 AND r.round = (SELECT MAX(round) FROM races WHERE year = 2009)
  ORDER BY ds.position ASC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT lt.lap, lt.time
FROM laptimes lt
JOIN races r ON lt.raceid = r.raceid
JOIN champion c ON lt.driverid = c.driverid
WHERE r.year = 2009
ORDER BY lt.milliseconds ASC
LIMIT 1
answer: The 2009 champion was Jenson Button (driverId 18). His fastest lap of the 2009 season was lap number 46, with a time of 1:14.353.
assumptions: The 2009 champion is determined as the driver with position=1 in driverstandings at the last round (round=17) of the 2009 season.
'Fastest lap' means the lap with minimum milliseconds among all laps this driver recorded in 2009 races (across all races, not just one).

final_sql:
SELECT AVG(CAST(r.fastestlapspeed AS REAL)) AS avg_fastest_lap_speed
FROM results r
JOIN races ra ON r.raceid = ra.raceid
WHERE ra.name = 'Spanish Grand Prix' AND ra.year = 2009
answer: The average fastest lap speed in the 2009 Spanish Grand Prix was approximately 199.64 km/h.
assumptions: Rows with null fastestlapspeed are excluded from the average, as is standard for AVG().
Only considered the race explicitly named 'Spanish Grand Prix' in year 2009 (not other Spain-related races).

final_sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT r.driverid, r.laps, d.dob
  FROM results r
  JOIN races ra ON ra.raceid = r.raceid
  JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = r.driverid
  WHERE ra.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2005
)
SELECT
  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM dob) < 1985 AND laps > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*) AS pct
FROM base;
answer: Among all race-result records for races held between 2000 and 2005, about 64.88% involve drivers born before 1985 who completed more than 50 laps (1,323 out of 2,039 total driver-race entries).
assumptions: Counting is done per results row (driver-race entry), not per distinct driver, following the hint's formula literally.
'laps' refers to results.laps (laps completed in that race).
Year of race (races.year) between 2000 and 2005 inclusive defines the race period.

Bundesliga, Italy Serie A, Netherlands Eredivisie, Poland Ekstraklasa, Portugal Liga ZON Sagres, Scotland Premier League, Spain LIGA BBVA, and Switzerland Super League.

Averages computed as SUM(goals)/COUNT(DISTINCT match id) as specified in the hint

SELECT CAST(AVG(l.alb) AS REAL) AS avg_alb
FROM laboratory l
JOIN patient p ON l.id = p.id
WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND l.plt > 400 AND p.diagnosis = 'SLE'
answer: The average blood albumin level (ALB) for female patients with a platelet count (PLT) greater than 400 who were diagnosed with SLE is approximately 3.91.
assumptions: Patient and laboratory records are joined on id, matching each patient's diagnosis and sex with all their lab records (not just a single visit).

final_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN l.pt >= 14 AND p.sex='F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN l.pt >= 14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pct
FROM patient p
JOIN laboratory l ON p.id = l.id
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - EXTRACT(YEAR FROM p.birthday) > 55
answer: Among patients older than 55 years old with abnormal prothrombin time (PT >= 14), about 78.36% are female (sex = 'F').
assumptions: Age is computed as the difference between the current year and the birth year (per the hint), not exact age in years.
Patient age > 55 is joined with laboratory records via patient id, using all lab records (not just latest) that meet PT >= 14 criteria.

final_sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.id) AS patient_count
FROM laboratory l
JOIN examination e ON l.id = e.id
WHERE l.igg > 900 AND l.igg < 2000
  AND e.symptoms IS NOT NULL;
answer: Only 1 patient has both a normal Ig G level (IGG between 900 and 2000) and a recorded symptom (non-null Symptoms field).
assumptions: Patients are identified by matching laboratory.id to examination.id (the only common key linking IGG lab results to Symptoms).

A patient counts if any of their lab records shows normal IGG and their examination record has non-null Symptoms; since examination has only 106 rows versus laboratory's 13908, most laboratory records have no matching examination record and are excluded.
'have symptoms' means the Symptoms field is not null, as stated in the hint, regardless of its text content.
